questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
A valve that prevents a truck from being stolen
A valve that prevents the driver from driving too fast

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak. The valve closes automatically when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: In a combination rig, it is best to make:
questions.explanation: When driving a combination vehicle, brake early and look far ahead to avoid sudden stops. This helps prevent your trailer from jackknifing.

questions.question: What is off-tracking?

options.text: When a vehicle's front wheels follow a different path than its rear wheels
When a vehicle's wheels all follow the same path
When a load shifts during a turn
When a vehicle's wheels run over a curb during a turn

questions.correctAnswerText: When a vehicle's front wheels follow a different path than its rear wheels
questions.explanation: When a vehicle turns a corner, the rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels. This is called off-tracking.

questions.question: When braking with a trailer that has anti-lock brakes, you should:

options.text: Use extra braking force to make sure the brakes work
Brake as you would without anti-lock brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake as you would without anti-lock brakes
questions.explanation: When driving a tractor-trailer with anti-lock brakes, brake the same way you would without anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: A driver should test the tractor protection valve by:

options.text: Releasing air with the brake pedal

questions.correctAnswerText: Releasing air with the brake pedal
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, let the air supply charge fully, turn off the engine, then press the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to its emergency position when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: Pushing in the trailer air supply control will:
questions.explanation: Push in the trailer air supply control to supply air to the trailer. Pull it out to turn off the air supply and activate the emergency brakes.

questions.question: When should the trailer hand valve be used?

options.text: Only when the trailer is carrying a load
Only to test the trailer's brakes
Only in bad weather when the trailer may skid

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer's brakes
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve is used to test the trailer brakes. Do not use it while the vehicle is moving, as it could cause a skid.

questions.question: What happens when the wheels of a trailer lock up?

options.text: The trailer will often continue to move in a straight line

questions.explanation: When a trailer's wheels lock up, the trailer may swing out and hit other vehicles. This is especially likely with lightly loaded trailers.

questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open
The rear shut-off valves should be open
All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves
No shut-off valves should be open

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves
questions.explanation: When starting a trip, open all shut-off valves except the last ones on the rear trailer. This allows air to reach all brakes and prevents air from escaping from the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Stay in the cab and call for help
Exit the cab and walk away from the tracks
Signal another driver to push your vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the cab and walk away from the tracks
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, exit the vehicle immediately and walk away from the tracks. Call emergency authorities for help.

questions.question: What color identifies service lines on air brake systems?
questions.explanation: Air lines use color codes to help drivers connect brake lines correctly. Blue identifies service lines. Red identifies emergency lines.

questions.question: When a combination vehicle is lightly loaded, what happens?

options.text: Should be loaded with most of the weight in the rear of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Lightly loaded vehicles have poor traction. The wheels can lock up easily when stopping, reducing braking power.

questions.question: Why do combination vehicles need extra road space?

options.text: They drive more slowly than other commercial vehicles.
They are heavier than other commercial vehicles.
They need more space to turn and stop than other commercial vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more space to turn and stop than other commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are longer. They require more space to turn and stop safely. Manage your space carefully when driving these vehicles.

questions.question: The service air line connects to which part?
questions.explanation: The service air line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It connects to relay valves, which apply trailer brakes quickly.

questions.question: What happens when an air supply control is set to "emergency"?
questions.explanation: When set to "emergency," the air supply stops and trailer emergency brakes apply immediately. Some older vehicles use levers instead of knobs for this control.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The tractor protection valve will close.
The rear trailer will detach from the combination.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tractor protection valve will close.
questions.explanation: The tractor protection valve protects the trailer's brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak. Loss of air pressure in the emergency line causes the valve to close and trailer emergency brakes to activate.

questions.question: What should you do before starting a trip?

options.text: Leave the service line valve open.

questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency and service line shut-off valves and listen for air escaping. This checks that all brakes work. Then close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers occur when drivers turn or change lanes too quickly.

questions.question: Which vehicle is most prone to the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are most likely to rollover from the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: What happens when a load is placed on one side of a trailer?

options.text: May add extra support during turns.
May be easier to steer during turns.

questions.explanation: Putting weight on one side of a trailer causes it to lean that way. This increases the risk of rollover during turns and lane changes.
